**🔥 TRENDING**  
*(none today – all stories are steady updates)*

### 🌐 AZURE INFRA  
**⭐ 1. AKS Release 2026‑09‑04** – Starting Sep 30, deprecated Availability‑Set clusters will auto‑migrate to VM‑based AKS nodes; plan migrations now to avoid service interruption. 🔗 https://github.com/Azure/AKS/releases/tag/2026-09-04  
**⭐ 2. Generally Available: User‑bound user‑delegation SAS for Azure Storage** – SAS tokens must be tied to a specific Entra ID, tightening storage access control for compliance. 🔗 https://azure.microsoft.com/updates?id=569241  
**3. Adding network intelligence into a network‑ready Azure migration plan** – Embedding network‑aware design into lift‑and‑shift migrations reduces latency and security gaps for VMware workloads moving to Azure. 🔗 https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/t5/azure-networking-blog/adding-network-intelligence-into-a-network-ready-azure-migration/ba-p/4554519  
**4. TLS/SSL certificate support for Azure Functions Flex Consumption** – Site‑scoped certificates on Flex Consumption plans simplify HTTPS compliance for serverless apps. 🔗 https://azure.microsoft.com/updates?id=570940  
**5. Azure Ephemeral OS Disk with full caching** – Caches the full OS image locally on VMs/VMSS, cutting boot‑time I/O and lowering storage costs. 🔗 https://azure.microsoft.com/updates?id=570551  

---

### 🛡️ AZURE SECURITY & IDENTITY  
**⭐ 1. Detect and disrupt AI‑themed attacks with Microsoft Defender** – Defender now auto‑detects AI‑driven phishing, malware and multi‑stage campaigns, helping block novel threats. 🔗 https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/09/10/detect-and-disrupt-ai-themed-attacks-with-microsoft-defender/  
**⭐ 2. Threat matrix: Mapping threats across cloud web applications** – New MITRE‑aligned matrix lets you prioritize mitigations for serverless and web‑app attack paths. 🔗 https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/09/09/threat-matrix-mapping-threats-across-cloud-web-applications/  
**3. Protecting organizations from AI‑assisted executive impersonation and invoice fraud** – Details a BEC campaign that used AI‑generated voices and fake invoices to steal ACH payments, underscoring MFA and anomaly detection. 🔗 https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/09/10/protecting-organizations-ai-assisted-executive-impersonation-invoice-fraud/  
**4. Passkey‑themed social engineering leads to identity and cloud compromise** – Shows how attackers abuse passkey phishing to gain MFA persistence and access SharePoint/OneDrive, with detection guidance. 🔗 https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/09/09/passkey-themed-social-engineering-leads-identity-cloud-compromise/  

---

### ⚙️ CLOUD & DEVOPS  
**1. GitHub’s August outages show growth outpacing infrastructure** – Rapid adoption of Actions and Copilot strained GitHub’s backend, a caution for scaling CI/CD pipelines. 🔗 https://devops.com/githubs-august-outages-show-growth-is-outpacing-infrastructure/  
**2. GitHub widens Advanced Security trials to 300 licenses** – Makes automated code scanning and secret detection more accessible for midsize enterprises. 🔗 https://devops.com/github-widens-the-door-on-advanced-security-trials/  
**3. How AWS Lambda logs every flow with eBPF and Rust** –
spokenText:
Good morning! Here is your daily brief for today.

First, Azure updates. Starting at the end of September, Azure Kubernetes Service will automatically migrate any remaining Availability Set clusters to VM based nodes, so plan your migrations now to avoid interruption. Azure Storage introduces user bound delegation for SAS tokens, tying each token to a specific Entra ID for tighter compliance. A new guidance adds network intelligence to lift‑and‑shift migrations, helping reduce latency and security gaps for VMware workloads moving to Azure. Azure Functions on Flex Consumption now support TLS and SSL certificates at the site level, simplifying HTTPS compliance for serverless apps. Finally, Azure offers an Ephemeral OS Disk with full caching, which stores the entire operating system image locally on VMs and scale sets, cutting boot time I/O and lowering storage costs.

Moving on to security and identity. Microsoft Defender has been enhanced to automatically detect AI‑driven phishing, malware and multi‑stage attacks, giving organizations a stronger shield against emerging threats. A new MITRE aligned threat matrix maps attack paths across cloud web applications, helping teams prioritize mitigations for serverless and web workloads. There is also a report on AI‑assisted business email compromise that uses synthetic voices and fake invoices to steal ACH payments, underscoring the need for multi‑factor authentication and anomaly detection. Additionally, attackers are exploiting passkey phishing to gain persistent access to SharePoint and OneDrive, with guidance on detection and response.

Now for cloud and DevOps news. GitHub experienced outages in August as rapid growth in Actions and Copilot usage strained its infrastructure, a reminder to design CI/CD pipelines with scalability in mind. GitHub is also expanding its Advanced Security trial to three hundred licenses, making automated code scanning and secret detection more accessible for midsize enterprises. Finally, AWS Lambda is now logging every request flow using eBPF and Rust, providing deeper visibility into serverless execution.

Bottom line: Azure is rolling out several important infrastructure and security features, AI‑driven threats are becoming more sophisticated, and cloud developers should stay vigilant about scaling and observability. That is your update. Have a great day!
